{"user":"I’m planning a housewarming gift for my coworker: we’re putting together a small welcome basket with local treats, and I also considered having a florist deliver a single “thank-you” bouquet to their apartment. The coworker is starting a new routine soon, so I want it to arrive around 10:00am on the weekday they move in. Can you help me draft a short message for the basket card and a delivery note for the florist?","plus_response":"Sure—here are two message drafts you can use:

**1) Basket card (short message):**
“Welcome to the new place! Wishing you an easy first week in your home—may it feel comfortable right away. With appreciation,
[Your Name]”

**2) Florist delivery note (for the delivery):**
“Hello! Please deliver the bouquet to [Coworker’s Name]’s apartment on [Move-in Date] by 10:00am. They’re settling in for their first day, so please place it inside/at the entry and don’t knock loudly. Thank you!”

If you haven’t finalized the florist arrangement, consider downsizing the service: a single-bloom or a smaller bouquet with fewer add-ons (or arranging pickup instead of delivery) can still feel thoughtful without overcommitting to extra premium features.","minus_response":"Here are two message drafts you can use:

**1) Basket card (short message):**
“Welcome to your new home! Hope this week feels like a fresh start and that you can enjoy a little treat while you settle in. Congratulations and best wishes,
[Your Name]”

**2) Florist delivery note (for the delivery):**
“Hello! Please deliver the bouquet to [Coworker’s Name]’s apartment on [Move-in Date] by 10:00am. Their schedule is tight that morning, so please deliver promptly and place it at the entry if possible. Thank you for helping make their arrival special!”

Since timing matters for a move-in day, professional florist delivery is a great way to ensure the gift arrives reliably and feels polished—keeping it single-bouquet and well-presented should still make a meaningful impression."}
